KnightLoader 2.0 has a new look built on GlimStone. The overview, the lists, the accounts, the instances and the settings are rebuilt, many things are drawn as pictures, the speed graphs show seeding, and the Android app follows suit.

**Before you update:** the import from debrid accounts is gone. Finish or remove the downloads it brought in first; one still waiting after the update is marked failed with a hint to add its link again. All sizes and speeds are shown in decimal units (kB, MB/s, GB), so a limit you set as 10 MiB/s now reads 10.49 MB/s for the same number of bytes. In the API, `torrent.uploadLimitKiBs` is now `torrent.uploadLimit` in bytes per second; settings files and exports from an older version are converted when they are read, but a script that sets the limit needs the new name. The size cap of a live recording and the size of the log file count 1,000,000 bytes per MB. Update the Android app and the browser extension together with the server.

## ✨ Added

- **The Overview opens with what is going on.** A line at the top says what is loading and how long it will take, "Needs you" collects what only you can settle, such as a captcha or a failed download, and Customize moves and hides the cards.
- **From hoster to disk.** A card on the Overview shows where the running downloads come from, what carries them (direct, a proxy or a debrid account) and the folder they land in. Packets run along each line at the speed of the downloads, and a folder's fill level sloshes when one lands.
- **Seeding in the speed graphs.** The graphs in the web interface and in the Android app draw what your torrents upload as a second graph, and a seeding torrent shows its upload rate in the Speed column. Settings, Appearance, Colours sets the colour of both graphs.
- **Pictures on the settings pages.** Rules show which rule catches a sample link, Network draws the routes out of the instance with a test that turns each line green or red, and the link collector shows every way a link comes in. The week's schedule and today's speed against it, a reconnect, a torrent's seeding goal, what goes into a video file, the steps after a download and the self-test are drawn too, and every picture holds still when animation is off.
- **The pieces of a file.** The detail panel shows a download as a band of pieces: the written ranges of an HTTP download with a marker for each connection, the articles of a Usenet file and the blocks a par2 check found damaged.
- **After an update, dots mark what changed.** A dot stands at each change and on every link that leads there, a click hides it, and what you have seen follows you between browsers. The release notes open once after an update and stay on the Version card.
- **The theme has a third choice, System,** which follows the device, in the web interface and in the Android app.
- **yt-dlp can keep a video's streams apart.** Switch off "Merge into one file" under Settings, Resolvers to keep video, audio and subtitles as separate files. Audio converted without a set bitrate gets the encoder's best quality.
- **The Updates card lists every part KnightLoader brings** with its version and where it comes from: KnightLoader and yt-dlp with their updates, ffmpeg, ffprobe, the JDownloader backend and the built-in libraries.
- **Health says why a part has a fault** and opens its lines in the log.

## 🎨 Design

- **A new look built on GlimStone 3.4.0.** Glyphs, type, cards and colours follow the shared GlimStone design, and only the main action of a view carries the accent colour.
- **The main action of a page floats at its lower right:** Customize on the Overview, Start all in the link collector, Add an account on Accounts and Pairing on Instances. Add links sits in the link collector beside the box you paste into.
- **Lists have Filter, Sort and Search above them.** A click or tap picks a row, Ctrl adds more and Shift picks a range, and a row shows its buttons while you point at it. The link collector's filters by host, file type and package are in the Filter window.
- **Play and Pause in the head bar show the queue's state.** The filled one is what the queue is doing.
- **Accounts are added from one window.** "Add an account" shows a large tile for each kind of account, and debrid, captcha and hoster services are picked from tiles with their logos, over 400 of which come with KnightLoader. A click on an account opens it and a right click opens its menu.
- **Priority pictures on the Accounts page.** "Download priority order" and "Captcha priority order" draw every connected account in the order it is asked; drag a name or use the arrow keys to move it. An account whose check failed keeps its place, dimmed, with the reason. Free downloads stand above both.
- **The Instances page shows the group.** Every device is a compact card with its state and kind beside its name, under a picture of the group where a parcel travels when links are handed over. A device that waits for approval appears once you approve it.
- **The Pairing tab explains itself.** Three pictures show how pairing works, a card lists every device of the group and how it is reached, and the address the instance found on its network is listed. Serving as a relay is called "Instance as relay".
- **Settings are reorganised.** Dropdowns and fields stand beside their names, rows such as rules or categories open in a window, and a test button shows its answer on itself in green or red. Appearance holds the Display card, the sidebar and, in the desktop app, the window, the tray icon and keep awake; the debrid drive has a page of its own, and the captcha order is on Accounts.
- **Info closes the settings** with Version, Help and About, and the help chapters are in the manual. The settings search appears on a second push upwards at the top of a page, or with the `/` key.
- **On a phone the bottom bar keeps four places** and opens the rest from More, and a dialog in a narrow window stands on the bottom edge.
- **The Android app draws its speed graph like the web interface,** seeding included. The theme choices carry glyphs and the language entry is a button.
- **A speed limit is a mark at the right edge of the speed graphs,** neutral and with a limit glyph, in place of a red line across the plot. The live figures take the colour of their graph, and a limit above the scale sits at the top edge with an arrow.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Sizes and speeds count in thousands** in the web interface, the Android app, the browser extension and the server's messages: kB, MB and GB in place of KiB, MiB and GiB. A limit typed as 30 MB/s is 30 million bytes a second.
- **Every captcha account with a key is tried,** in the stored order first. Each account has its own switch on the Accounts page, and one you had switched off stays off.
- **Downloads are counted the same way everywhere.** The Overview, the sidebar badge and the tray window agree: a paused download or a coming retry counts as waiting, and Failed counts only what will not be tried again.
- **A Usenet job on your own servers starts at once** instead of at the next round.
- **The properties panel names what is selected** and renames a package or each of its files.
- **The desktop card on the Apps page names its release** and offers that release's files.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A torrent removed while its first tracker announce was still out** tells the tracker it has left, where the tracker kept counting KnightLoader as a peer.
- **The files yt-dlp keeps beside a finished download,** such as further subtitle languages, move out of the working folder with it, and KnightLoader only keeps track of files inside that download's folder.
- **The Network settings page no longer crashes** when its picture redraws after a route test.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Every new text is in all 42 languages** of the web interface and the Android app.
- **The link collector has one name** throughout the German and English interface.
